title: Why Should We Use Debouncing in React?
excerpt: Every time a user types a letter, the application sends an API request to search for products.
body:
ㅤ
📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 16
ㅤ
Imagine you're building an e-commerce application with a search bar.

Every time a user types a letter, the application sends an API request to search for products.

If someone types "laptop", that's potentially six API requests for a single search.

It works, but is it really necessary?

This is where debouncing becomes useful.
ㅤ
1️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝘀 𝗗𝗲𝗯𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴?

Debouncing is a technique that delays an operation until a certain amount of time has passed since the last event.

Instead of making an API request after every keystroke, we wait until the user stops typing for a short period.

For example, with a 500ms delay:

Without Debouncing:
L → LA → LAP → LAPT → LAPTO → LAPTOP

6 potential API requests.

With Debouncing:
User types "LAPTOP" → Wait 500ms → Send request

Just 1 API request if the user types continuously.
ㅤ
2️⃣ 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗜𝘁 𝗶𝗻 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗰𝘁

We can implement a simple debounce using useEffect and setTimeout.

Example:

const [search, setSearch] = useState("");
const [debouncedSearch, setDebouncedSearch] = useState("");

useEffect(() => {
  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    setDebouncedSearch(search);
  }, 500);

  return () => clearTimeout(timer);
}, [search]);

Here, whenever the search value changes, the previous timer is cleared.

Only after 500ms without another change will debouncedSearch update.

We can then use debouncedSearch to trigger our search API request.
ㅤ
3️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗗𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗜𝘁 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿?

Debouncing can help us:

• Reduce unnecessary API requests
• Lower backend processing overhead
• Avoid repeated expensive operations
• Improve the search experience

It's particularly useful for search suggestions, autocomplete, and filtering large datasets.
ㅤ
4️⃣ 𝗢𝗻𝗲 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗼 𝗥𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿

Debouncing doesn't automatically handle every API-related issue.

For real applications, we should also consider cancelling outdated requests or preventing older responses from replacing newer results.
ㅤ
𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

Small improvements can make a noticeable difference in how an application performs.

Debouncing is a simple technique, but knowing when to use it can help us build more efficient and user-friendly React applications.

Sometimes, better performance isn't about doing things faster. It's about avoiding unnecessary work.
ㅤ
